## Project Overview

[GitHub Repository ⇒](https://github.com/kacp3rrr/citibike-spatiotemporal-analysis)

Analysis and prediction of NYC CitiBike ridership patterns using historical trip data, weather observations, and geospatial neighborhood data across April-June 2024

This project aggregates ~5 million individual trips into hourly station-level counts, merged with weather and spatial data. This dataset is then analyzed and used to build predictive models to understand what drives ridership demand.

## Navigation

Use the navbar above to explore each phase of the analysis:

- **Pipeline**: data loading, aggregation, spatial joins, weather merge
- **EDA**: temporal, geographic, weather, and behavioral patterns  
- **Modeling**: feature engineering, model comparison, spatial residuals
- **Maps**: choropleth, bubble map, flow imbalance

## Key Findings

| Finding | Value |
|---|---|
| Rain ridership reduction | 16.5% |
| Rush hour multiplier | 1.40x |
| Electric bike share | 65% |
| Best model R² | 0.192 |
| Baseline RMSE improvement | 10.35% |
| Pier 61 flow imbalance | 6x network average |

## Dataset

- ~5 million CitiBike trips aggregated to 1.9M hourly station observations
- 2,289 active stations across NYC
- Merged with NOAA hourly weather and NYC geospatial neighborhood data

## Data Sources

- [CitiBike System Data](https://citibikenyc.com/system-data)
- [NOAA Local Climatological Data](https://ncei.noaa.gov/cdo-web/)
- [NYC Open Data](https://opendata.cityofnewyork.us/)
